title: Garlicky Shrimp, Spinach, and White Bean Quesadillas
intro: This satisfying lunch comes together quickly when you need a filling meal to power through the afternoon. The creamy bean mash holds everything together while delivering a substantial fiber boost without heavy melted cheese.

ingredients.name: No-salt-added canned cannellini beans
ingredients.canonical_name: Beans, white, mature seeds, canned, without salt

instructions: Place the frozen shrimp in a bowl of cold water to thaw for 5 minutes. Drain the water, pull off any tails, and chop the shrimp.
Mash the cannellini beans, lemon juice, garlic powder, and dried oregano in a medium bowl until mostly smooth.
Lay the tortillas flat on a clean surface. Spread the bean mash evenly over one half of each tortilla to create a thick base.
Press the chopped shrimp, fresh spinach, and crumbled feta cheese into the bean mash. Fold the bare half over to close the quesadillas.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and brush the surface with the extra-virgin olive oil.
Add the quesadillas to the skillet. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the bottoms are golden brown and crisp.
Flip the quesadillas and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp and the spinach wilts. Cut into wedges and serve.
variation: Trade the shrimp for cooked, shredded skinless chicken breast.
conservation: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.

Based on the specified ingredients (260g beans, two 45g whole-wheat tortillas, 170g shrimp, 20g feta), the per-serving values should realistically sit around 400 kcal, 53g carbs, and 2.5g saturated fat, which all fall well within the 'main' chapter targets. The recipe itself is portioned correctly; investigate the underlying database mapping for the tortillas or beans.
